rationale: The Court is likely to issue a narrow Roberts opinion holding that MVRA restitution, when retroactively increased by statutory amendment for pre-enactment conduct, functions as criminal punishment under the intent-effects/Mendoza-Martinez framework and thus triggers the Ex Post Facto Clause. Thomas and Gorsuch are the most likely to write separate concurrences emphasizing original meaning/anti-evasion principles, while Alito is likely to dissent stressing Hudson/Smith’s “clearest proof” standard and administrability concerns.
